ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is vertical line segment AE, and on the right side is vertical line segment DC; both have arrow markings in the same direction, indicating AE ∥ DC. The two slanted lines AC and ED intersect at point B. The figure labels AB = x + 3, BC = 2x - 8, EB = 5, and BD = 3. The problem asks to find AB. Reasoning: Because AE ∥ DC, and AC and ED intersect at point B, triangle ABE and triangle CBD are similar by AA. The corresponding sides are AB ↔ CB and EB ↔ DB. Therefore AB/CB = EB/DB. Substituting the labels in the figure gives (x + 3)/(2x - 8) = 5/3. Cross multiply: 3(x + 3) = 5(2x - 8), that is, 3x + 9 = 10x - 40, so 49 = 7x, x = 7. Thus AB = x + 3 = 7 + 3 = 10.
